summary: Sub-second timestamp skew in scheduled batch jobs causing hourly billing fragmentation and duplicate invoice lines
description:
Issue summary:
KiteAI reports duplicate invoice lines for the same hourly window after nightly scheduled batch runs. Investigation shows some batch job postbacks are landing with sub-second timestamp offsets (milliseconds) that push a subset of events into the previous hour bucket, causing the system to split the same job’s usage across two hourly billing lines.

Impact:
- Customer sees two invoice line items for a single scheduled job; total token counts match expected but split across two rate tiers (hourly smoothing applied separately).
- Confusing billing UI and automated reconciliation for finance teams (client accounting flagged as discrepancy).
- Affects reconciliations for customers relying on hourly-aggregated reserved credits.

Environment:
- Dedicated organization: KiteAI (org id masked)
- Scheduled batch job: nightly-embeddings job triggered at 02:00:00.000 UTC
- Region: us-east
- Ingress path: edge-proxy -> batch-ingest -> metering-postback

Steps to reproduce:
1. Schedule a batch job to start exactly on the hour (02:00:00.000 UTC) in dedicated cluster.
2. Observe postback timestamps for microbatches from two edge proxies handling the job.
3. One proxy emits postbacks at 01:59:59.998-01:59:59.999 (millisecond skew) while the other emits at 02:00:00.001-02:00:00.010.
4. Metering aggregator assigns usage to hourly buckets using raw timestamps; subset gets bucketed into previous hour leading to two invoice lines for the same job window.

Observed logs/snippets:
- batch-ingest logs show microbatch finish times within +-12ms across proxies.
- metering service debug: "assign_bucket": "2026-03-13T01:59:59.999Z" vs "2026-03-13T02:00:00.002Z"
- invoice lines: hour 01:00-02:00 -> 80k tokens, hour 02:00-03:00 -> 20k tokens (both attributed to same job id).

Expected behavior:
- Events from a single job that straddle sub-second boundaries should be coherent for hourly aggregation, either via consistent rounding rules or by using job-window alignment metadata rather than raw event timestamp.

Workaround used by Support/Customer:
- Created a temporary reconciliation script to merge the two hourly lines for the job and requested provisional credit/adjustment while engineering investigates.
comments: 2026-03-14 09:12 - Customer (KiteAI Billing): We noticed two line items for last night's embeddings run; totals line up but split broke reconciliation. Can you advise?
2026-03-14 09:28 - Support (Jasmine): Thanks — opened ticket SUP-110311 and escalated to billing engineering. Please provide job id and any correlated invoice IDs.

2026-03-14 10:05 - Engineering (Marco): Preliminary logs show millisecond skew between edge proxies. Metering currently buckets by raw timestamp without rounding. Hypothesis: sub-second skew causes fragmentation.
2026-03-14 13:42 - Billing Ops (Lina): Applied provisional credit to KiteAI for the split line (reference memo #CR-2026-0314). Awaiting engineering fix for root cause.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis: Multiple edge proxies and clock/latency differences cause sub-second variance. Metering aggregation logic uses raw RFC3339 timestamps and floors to hour boundaries; no explicit subsecond normalization. Potential fixes: 1) canonicalize timestamps to seconds when assigning hourly buckets; 2) prefer job-window metadata (job_start, job_end) to attribute all microbatches to job window; 3) add short reconcile pass for events within +/-50ms of boundary to prefer majority bucket. Need perf impact analysis for solution 2. Related infra: NTP/chrony drift appears nominal but request tracing shows network microburst delays.
resolution: Provisionally credited customer for split lines (memo CR-2026-0314). Engineering to ship a metering patch that rounds timestamps to second precision when assigning hourly buckets; target hotfix in next maintenance window with telemetry to detect any remaining fragmentation. Post-deploy: run reconciliation job to auto-merge split lines for affected jobs and issue final invoice adjustments for the prior 7 days. Follow-up task created INT-110412 to audit edge proxy timestamp sources and NTP config across dedicated fleets.
fix_plan:
1) Backport quick patch to metering service to normalize timestamps to second precision for hourly bucketing (low risk)
2) Add job-window attribution logic as a medium-term fix (requires schema changes)
3) Run 7-day retrospective reconciliation and issue invoice credits where appropriate
4) Audit edge proxy time sync and deploy NTP hardening if needed
public_notes_for_customer: We've applied a provisional credit and are deploying a low-risk metering patch to avoid future splits. We will reconcile the last 7 days and follow up when the hotfix is live.
private_notes: Watch for increased metering spikes after normalization; ensure reconciliation job de-duplicates by job_id to avoid double-crediting. Coordinate with billing-ops before auto-applying credits beyond provisional memo.
